title: H37Rv as a coordinate system
dek: 4.4 Mb, ~4,000 genes, GC-rich, reference — not a clinical median. Essentials, PE/PPE, and the repeats you mask are why distances and DST calls move.
story: H37Rv (Cole 1998 and later assemblies) is the coordinate system: ~4.41 Mb, ~65% GC, ~4,000 annotated coding sequences, Rv numbering. Clinical isolates are not H37Rv with a few SNPs; they are a clonal species with lineage-defining distances of hundreds of SNPs and accessory PE/PPE flux.

Essentiality is condition-dependent. Saturated transposon screens (TraSH, Himar1 Tn-seq) mark a few hundred genes as required on rich plates; macrophage, hypoxia, and mouse spleens move that set. KatG is dispensable on plates and essential for INH activation — essentiality is not the same as clinical importance.

PE/PPE genes, IS6110 copies, and GC-rich repeats are the masking problem. Unmasked SNP distances inflate relatedness metrics. Under-called pncA or Rv0678 in low-complexity sequence is a DST problem. The reference is a map; it is not the patient.
deepTitle: What to keep in a gDST BAM header
deep: Always state the reference build (H37Rv NC_000962.3 is still the common DST coordinate). M. bovis BCG Pasteur is the wrong reference for a pulmonary Mtb.
IS6110 copy number varies by lineage (often higher in L2). Ultra’s IS6110/IS1081 extra sensitivity is a copy-number gift, not a new species.
Core genome alignments for transmission typically mask PE/PPE, repeats, and drug-resistance genes if you do not want treatment to look like phylogeny. Say what you masked.

Essential-gene lists are priors for interpreting loss-of-function. A frameshift in a Tn-seq-essential gene in a viable isolate is contamination, mixed mapping, or a wrong essentiality prior — worth a look at the BAM.

example.title: SNP distance 12 after unmasking PE/PPE
example.setup: Two household isolates: 12 SNPs unmasked, 3 SNPs after standard PE/PPE/repeat mask. Health department wants a transmission cluster call.

steps.title: Ask what was masked
steps.body: PE/PPE mapping error is not evolution. Unmasked distances are not a physical constant.

steps.title: Use the lab’s SOP threshold on the masked alignment
steps.body: If your programme clusters at ≤5–12 masked SNPs, these two belong together. Do not mix thresholds across pipelines.

steps.title: Keep DST genes out of phylogeny if they are under selection
steps.body: Independent acquisition of S450L can collapse two unrelated strains in an unmasked tree.

example.takeaway: Distance is a method, not a fact of nature.

check.prompt: H37Rv in a DST pipeline is best treated as:
choices: The infecting strain in most patients
A coordinate system and annotation set, not a clinical median isolate
Proof that PE/PPE genes do not exist
check.answer: A coordinate system and annotation set, not a clinical median isolate
check.why: Patients have lineages. H37Rv is the map.

whyWrong.The infecting strain in most patients: L4 lab strain, not a global median.

check.prompt: H37Rv is ~4.41 Mb. At uniform 50× unique coverage, roughly how many haploid-genome bases are sampled?
check.why: 4.41e6 × 50 ≈ 2.2e8. Depth is not read count without length.

whyWrong.~4.4 × 10^3 bases: Off by the megabase and the depth.
whyWrong.50 bases: That is the depth, not the yield.

check.prompt: On the constellation plate, what is the pedagogical point of the term “not the patient”?
choices: That WGS should not be used
That the reference genome is a coordinate origin, not the clinical isolate
That PE/PPE genes should be copy-pasted from Mycobrowser into reports
check.answer: That the reference genome is a coordinate origin, not the clinical isolate
check.why: The caption states it. Masking and lineage exist because the patient is not H37Rv.

whyWrong.That PE/PPE genes should be copy-pasted: The user rule is the opposite.
